subject: Renewal sizing + incremental GPU add-on / throughput assurances
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlasai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated renewal — capacity uplift options

Hi Camila,

We’re starting renewal planning for our Dedicated pool (renewal due 2027-01-05) and evaluating a mid-term uplift to support a new vector search workload. Current pool: 120 GPUs (mixed A100/RTX), steady-state throughput ~85 ctx/sec across peak windows.

High level ask: can Redwood provide options for adding incremental GPUs mid-contract (50–100 GPU add-on), plus a pricing table showing committed reserved pricing vs burst credits and any volume/term discount bands. Also need throughput guarantees (or a SLO credit structure) for the blended pool — this workload is latency-sensitive.

Procurement timeline: we want commercial terms by 2026-11-15 and legal redlines by 2026-11-25. Please include any requirements for benchmarking/canary windows.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Jordan
VP, Infrastructure
AtlasAI

---
Attachment: procurement_request_form.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlasai.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated renewal — capacity uplift options

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. High level you have two clean paths we usually recommend:

1) Reserved step-up (recommended for predictable unit cost): commit to an incremental reserved tranche now (e.g., +50 GPUs on a 12-mo rider) with a staged onboarding at month 1 and month 4. This preserves a lower per-GPU effective rate and gives you throughput guarantees tied to the reserved pool.

2) Hybrid burst + short-term reserve: keep current commit, purchase burst credits for immediate headroom and place a smaller reserved top-up (25–50 GPUs) at renewal if utilization stabilizes. This gives flexibility but higher unit cost during the burst window.

I’ve attached a short sizing proposal and a pricing matrix that maps commit size → list price → example discount tiers. Key open items for us to size guarantees: target sustained tokens/sec (or ctx/sec), acceptable p95 tail latency, and whether you want cross-region fallback.

Proposed next step: if you can provide a 24-hour sample trace (token distribution + peak minutes/hour), we’ll run a quick throughput model and come back with an explicit quote and an SLA credit table.

I’ll loop in Aditya and Laura to confirm discount approval thresholds and DocuSign routing.

—Camila
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Camila.Reyes@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Date: 2026-11-03T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated renewal — capacity uplift options

Thanks Camila — attaching the 24-hour trace you requested (redacted) and our procurement notes. A few clarifications:

- Baseline: our steady-state target for the vector workload is 140 ctx/sec sustained during peak (previously 85). Peak p95 target = 220 ctx/sec.
- Risk tolerance: we can accept up to 10% p95 degradation during short bursts if compensated by credits.
- Residency: for compliance, the inference results and logs for this workload must remain in us-west-2.
- Discount ask: commercial would like to see a 15–20% effective discount on the incremental reserved tranche if we commit +50 GPUs for 12 months; higher if we can consolidate commit tiers.

Procurement attached: signed procurement_timeline.pdf and our standard redlines doc.

Jordan

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlasai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T11:27:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed commercial for Atlas — staged reserve + canary plan

Team / Jordan,

Thanks for the trace — we ran a quick throughput projection and a short internal soak. Summary proposal (provisional):

- Phase A (immediate): add +50 reserved GPUs as a 12-month rider (start date upon amendment signature). Effective discount: 18% off list for the tranche (requires signed amendment + 30-day payment term). Throughput guarantee: reserved tranche will provide baseline 150 ctx/sec sustained (per bench). SLA credit: 5% invoice credit per 1% below guaranteed p95 (capped at 25% monthly).
- Phase B (optional ramp at month 4): additional +50 GPUs (final size contingent on utilization). If you commit to Phase B at signing, we can improve the tranche discount to 21% on the full +100 tranche.
- Canary: a 14-day canary window after Phase A where we validate the integrated pool under your traffic. During the canary, we’ll run joint benchmarks and maintain an elevated support rotation. If throughput misses the guaranteed band, we will: (a) waive one month’s invoice for the incremental tranche and (b) provide a remediation runbook and priority optimization pass.

Open commercial ask: I need approval to commit to the 18% starter discount from Aditya/Laura (this is slightly beyond standard SA playbook). Also confirming we will restrict this pool to us-west-2 to satisfy your residency ask.

Next steps: Aditya — can you confirm whether we can approve the 18% for Phase A as a field exception? Laura — if yes, please draft ATLAS-QUOTE-20261104.pdf and prepare DocuSign routing for the amendment + rider. Jordan — if that looks good I’ll send a finalized quote and schedule the canary window.

—Camila

Camila / team — approved to offer a one-time field concession to 18% for Phase A only, subject to:

1) 30-day net payment term on the rider
2) DocuSign executed amendment by 2026-11-18
3) Canary metrics: Atlas to provide two benchmark runs within the 14-day window; if misses >10% on p95 we’ll enact the remediation commitments Camila outlined.

Note: I prefer the SLA credit be capped at a single monthly credit (not recurring) for operational simplicity — propose we reflect that in the quote. Laura, please bake that language into the quote and include the alternate SLA credit cap.

Aditya
